blind.location: p. 140 (PDF p. 6), Figure 2 caption; p. 139 exclusions
blind.quote: N = 158 nonvoters, 275 Clinton voters, and 218 Trump voters.
blind.sample_role: Respondents in the Figure 2 first-condition vote-choice analysis; three mutually exclusive final voter groups.
blind.exclusions: Third-party voters excluded from analysis (p. 139); only the first randomized question condition is represented. No further Figure 2 exclusions specified.

disposition.reason: Figure 2 explicitly gives three mutually exclusive final vote-choice groups for the first-condition outcome; sum represents all displayed voter groups. Third-party voters are excluded (p. 139). This is not a pooled binary effect estimate.
disposition.quote: N = 158 nonvoters, 275 Clinton voters, and 218 Trump voters.
disposition.calculation: 158 nonvoters + 275 Clinton voters + 218 Trump voters = 651 respondents. Clinton voters plus nonvoters comprise the displayed non-Trump groups; no new pooled effect is calculated.

worker_target_description: Study 1, first randomized condition: incorrect choice of image A as having more people, by 2016 vote choice (Trump voters, Clinton voters, nonvoters), Results/Figure 2. The original uses vote choice, not Republican party identification. No separate pooled binary non-Trump contrast is printed.
worker_notes: Analytic N arithmetic: 158 nonvoters + 275 Clinton voters + 218 Trump voters = 651 respondents. This is the full printed vote-choice comparison, not a pairwise Trump-versus-Clinton N and not the approval analysis. Weighted incorrect-response percentages are printed separately as 3 percent nonvoters, 2 percent Clinton voters and 15 percent Trump voters. No scalar comparative effect or named test statistic is printed; percentages were not converted into an effect. The same paragraph reports p < .01 for vote-choice/approval differences; p is unassigned here. Approval is a separate moderator and is not substituted for voter groups. Only assigned unfinished original fields were examined for output; other fields and replication/success are unassigned placeholders.

coding_context.description: Trump voters/Republicans select the incorrect inauguration crowd photo more often than non-Trump voters/non-Republicans
coding_context.reported_success_quote: We found that despite this delay the original result replicated, albeit with a smaller magnitude.
